Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support Sravan Bhaskaravajjula (@bhshravankumar) 7 months, 3 weeks ago Hello @lukafuka , Thank you for sharing your feedback. We’re sorry for any confusion caused. Google Calendar integration is currently part of the Pro version of LatePoint. On our plugin repository page, we’ve already included a clear Free vs Pro comparison link in the description section to help users understand the feature differences before installing, and we continuously work to keep this as transparent as possible. We completely understand how frustrating it can be if expectations don’t align with what you were looking for. Since discussing anything related to the pro version is not allowed in this forum [ https://wordpress.org/support/guidelines/#do-not-post-about-commercial-products ], if you’d like to explore the Pro functionality further, we’d be happy to provide access to a full Pro demo website so you can review how everything works. Please feel free to open a support ticket with us on https://wpdocs.latepoint.com/support/ , and our team will gladly assist you. We truly value your feedback and would appreciate the opportunity to clarify and improve your experience. Thank you again for taking the time to share your thoughts. It leaves dozens of tables in the database. Not sure why…. This topic was modified 8 months, 2 weeks ago by dan009 . Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support Sravan Bhaskaravajjula (@bhshravankumar) 7 months, 2 weeks ago Hello @dan009 , Allow me to share that starting from version 5.2.10, we have introduced a setting which, when enabled, ensures that the plugin tables are properly removed from the database upon deletion of the plugin. Here is the help article: https://latepoint.com/docs/how-to-remove-all-latepoint-data/ We kindly request you to please update to the latest version and test it once again. If everything works as expected on your end, we would truly appreciate it if you could consider updating your review accordingly.
